input.task: Show me the authoress who wrote the quote about thinking.

provenance: PR #42 R8 (MEDIUM), re-pointed at R13. R4's widening added `(?:name|list|give|show)(?: me)? the \w+s`, which read ANY singular noun ending in s as plural, so 'Show me the address of...', 'Name the business that...' and 'Show me the class of...' all began refusing a narrowing that used to work — a capability regression in the safe direction, undeclared, pinned by nothing. The exclusion that fixes it is `ss` and only `ss`: an English plural of a word ending in `ss` is `-sses`, so no plural carries `ss` immediately before its final s. This case's noun was `genius` for one round, and R13 falsified that — `us` cannot be excluded without losing `menus`, `gurus`, `bayous` — so it now uses an `-ss` noun, the only shape the rule can honestly protect. Watched red by ablation over the whole suite, with the exclusion dropped back to `\w+s`: `status failure:locate`, `3 matches at tier text`, for a singular task that must still narrow. Its twin `resolver-refuses-plural-menus` is red if the exclusion widens past `ss`, so neither direction can be traded for the other.

triage.what_this_grades: the OVER-firing direction of the plural test, which had no case at all — every other plural case grades under-firing. Red when the exclusion is removed, green with it, and the plural family stays green either way, so the two directions are pinned independently.
triage.ceiling: still a spelling rule, not a grammar, and now deliberately biased: every singular noun ending in any letter but `s` plus s — `the status`, `the genius`, `the analysis`, `the lens`, `the news` — reads as plural and refuses to narrow. That direction costs a loud `locate` failure; the opposite direction costs a confident wrong answer (R13), so the asymmetry is chosen rather than split. Declared as D28 (4).
